newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria's First East Intl Bank seeks merger.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria's First East Intl Bank seeks merger.

text.p: Bulgaria's private First East International Bank (FEIB) plans to seek a merger or to become part of a holding structure in a bid to expand its operations, FEIB's executive director said.

"The shareholders authorised on Tuesday the bank's managers to hold talks on a possible merger with other banks or on joining a holding structure," Anna Sabeva told reporters after a bank shareholders' meeting.
Sabeva declined to elaborate, saying that so far FEIB had held merger talks with several banks but had not come to a final agreement.
Local media reports said last month that FEIB was willing to join a larger structure led by state-owned Hebrosbank.
The projected institution was to manage financing of Bulgaria's agriculture and attract state funds for agriculture support, reports said.
By the end of August the FEIB's paid-in capital amounted to 2.1 billion levs.
The bank has a registered capital of 3.0 billion levs, distributed in voting shares worth two billion and one billion in non-voting stocks.
The shareholders authorised the supervisory board to decide on a capital rise up to seven billion levs through a new share issue within the next four years.
"The bank's capital-to-risk assets ratio stood at plus 0.79 percent," Sabeva said.
She declined to give further details of the bank's financial performance.

On September 23 the FEIB narrowly escaped being put under receivership by the central bank along with nine other banks by raising its capital-to-risk assets ratio through the sale of its stake in the local General Insurance Company.

Several months ago Bulgaria's tobacco monopolist Bulgartabac Holding became a shareholder in FEIB with 21.19 percent of its equity, which it acquired against an outstanding debt of a tobacco trading company to Bulgartabac guaranteed by FEIB.
